2027-02-01.title: Monday after Aneede Sunday
readings: Rescued from darkness into the kingdom of his beloved Son
Pray then in this way: Our Father
2027-02-01.alt: Season of Denho. Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple, is tomorrow; the Great Fast begins next week.
2027-02-01.verse: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
theo: Paul tells the Colossians that he never stops praying for them: “we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding, so that you may lead lives worthy of the Lord.” He prays that they may be “prepared to endure everything with patience, while joyfully giving thanks to the Father”, and then he names the great change that has already happened: “He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.” The Christian life is lived in that new kingdom, and it is learned in prayer.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches the prayer of that kingdom: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” Only one petition receives a commentary from the Lord himself, the one about forgiveness: “if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” Our Church prays the Lord’s Prayer at every hour of the Shehimo and before Holy Communion in the Qurbono. In a week the Great Fast will open with Shubkono, the service of mutual forgiveness. This week is the time to say the Our Father slowly and to ask: whom have I still not forgiven? St Cyprian of Carthage wrote that we call God “Father” together, not “my Father”, because we pray as one people and for one another (in substance).
outline: Ask: how many times did you say the Our Father last week, and did you mean the line about forgiveness?
Point 1 · Filled with the knowledge of his will
Point 3 · Forgive as you are forgiven
“Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
live: Say one Our Father today, pausing after each line.
Name one person you need to forgive before the Fast begins, and pray for them.
2027-02-01.prayer: Our Father in heaven, you rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of your beloved Son. Fill us with the knowledge of your will, teach us to pray as he taught us, and give us hearts that forgive, so that we may enter the Great Fast reconciled with you and with one another. Amen.
altar: Before Holy Communion we pray the Our Father together: forgiven and forgiving, we approach the one Bread.

quick: Paul prays that we may know God's will and live worthy of the Lord.
God has moved us from darkness into the kingdom of his Son.
Jesus teaches us to ask forgiveness as we forgive.
2027-02-01.action: Say one Our Father slowly today and pray for someone you need to forgive.
2027-02-01.question: Is there anyone whose name makes the line “as we forgive” hard for me to say?

family.explain: Jesus taught us his own prayer. We call God “our Father”, so we are all brothers and sisters. In the prayer we ask God to forgive us, and we promise to forgive others too.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is sad or hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to say sorry to, or forgive, this week?”

illus: A grandmother in Mavelikara taught her grandchildren the Our Father in Malayalam and in Syriac. One evening the boy stopped in the middle and refused to go on. His sister had broken his toy, he said, and he could not say ‘as we forgive’. The grandmother waited quietly. After a minute he went to his sister, shook her hand, came back and finished the prayer. She told him: now you have really prayed it.

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Teach us to pray. Amen.
share: Filled with the knowledge of God's will (Colossians 1:9). What do I ask for when I pray for others?
He has rescued us from the power of darkness (Colossians 1:13). Where have I seen his light this year?
As we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:12). Whom do I still need to forgive?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For our parish as it prepares for the Great Fast.
For families divided by quarrels over property or words.
For those who find it hard to forgive.
For the sick and the dying, and for the departed faithful we remembered on Sunday.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you ours. Make us one family that forgives, and lead us into the Fast with clean hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Colossians: we have not ceased praying for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will (Colossians 1:9). Before he teaches them anything, he prays for them.

Then he reminds them what God has done: he has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins (Colossians 1:13–14). We belong to a new kingdom.

In the Gospel Jesus gives us the prayer of that kingdom, the Our Father. Of all its lines he explains only one: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14).

Next Monday the Great Fast opens with Shubkono, when we ask one another for forgiveness. Let us use this week to say the Our Father slowly and to make peace with anyone we have not yet forgiven. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus gave us his own prayer, the Our Father. When we say it, we ask God to forgive us, and we promise to forgive others too. Is there someone you need to forgive today?

intro: Theme: “Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
A week before the Great Fast, the Church puts the Lord's Prayer in our hands.

points.h: Filled with the knowledge of his will
q: Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Let your good spirit lead me on a level path.
For this reason, since the day we heard it, we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
points.apply: Pray by name today for three people you love.

sub: His name, his kingdom, his will first.
q: Yet, O Lord, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly, once in the morning and once at night.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Make peace with one person before the Fast begins.

concl: We have been moved from darkness into the kingdom of the Son.
The prayer of that kingdom asks forgiveness and promises it.
2027-02-01.resolve: Before next Monday, forgive one person from the heart.
